feed.subtitle: Top stories in the U.S. and world news, politics, health, science, business, music, arts and culture. Nonprofit journalism with a mission. This is NPR.

entry.title: It was a big night for doctors to win seats in Congress, riding the blue wave
entry.summary: Historically, most physicians who served in the House or Senate have been Republicans. In the next Congress, physicians who are Democrats made significant gains.

entry.title: Navajo voters hop tractors, make extraordinary efforts to vote after widespread flooding
entry.summary: Four weeks of flooding washed out roads and sent thousands fleeing their homes on the Navajo Reservation. But many worked hard to get to polling places and voting day became part of the recovery process.

entry.title: Herbert Blomstedt, conductor of great orchestras for seven decades, dies at 99
entry.summary: Modest in his demeanor but remarkably enduring, the American-born, Swedish conductor continually fell in love with music, leading orchestras with no-nonsense insight and integrity well into his 90s.

entry.title: Chuck Schumer heralds Democrats' 'generational remake' of Senate
entry.summary: In remarks the day after his party flipped control of Congress, the Senate Minority Leader said voters had spoken clearly about their priorities, and said it's up to the Democratic party to deliver.

entry.title: Mike Johnson will step aside as top House Republican next Congress
entry.summary: After Tuesday's bruising defeat for Republicans, House Speaker Mike Johnson will not stay on as minority leader come January.

entry.title: Back in the majority, Democrats have plans for a long list of Trump investigations
entry.summary: Democrats will have the ability to subpoena records and compel individuals to testify. The Epstein files, Elon Musk, the Iran war and Trump's business interests may all come under the microscope.

entry.title: 'I was partying too much': Jordan Firstman knows firsthand about being a 'Club Kid'
entry.summary: Firstman's new film is about a gay party promoter whose life is upended when he discovers he has a young son. "Arlo teaches Peter to grow up, and I think Peter teaches Arlo to be a kid," he says.
